target.title: fix(net): cap default outbound HTTP connection pool limits
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Node.js `http.Agent` defaults `maxSockets` to `Infinity` per origin, and undici `Pool` leaves `connections` unbounded by default. Under high concurrency — a misbehaving proxy upstream, a surge of simultaneous outbound LLM API calls, or connection leaks — the process can exhaust OS socket limits.

The in-direction (Gateway WebSocket server) already has per-IP preauth connection budgets (`preauth-connection-budget.ts`). The out-direction had no equivalent guard.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add defensive defaults matching common industry practice:

| Setting | Before | After | Rationale |
|---------|--------|-------|-----------|
| undici Pool `connections` | unbounded | **256** | Per-origin cap for proxy client pools |
| Node `maxSockets` | `Infinity` | **256** | Per-origin socket cap; keepAlive Agent ~256 |
| Node `maxTotalSockets` | `Infinity` | **1024** | Global total cap; 4x per-origin |

Callers retain the ability to override via explicit `agentOptions` / `clientFactory` options.

## User Impact

- **Normal workloads**: no visible impact
- **High-concurrency agent fleets**: protected from OS-level socket exhaustion
- **Compatibility**: fully backward-compatible — explicit caller limits take precedence

## Evidence

- Tests pass locally for the changed surface:
  ```
  $ pnpm test src/infra/net/node-proxy-agent.test.ts src/infra/net/undici-runtime.test.ts -- --run
   ✓ 3 passed  (node-proxy-agent)
   ✓ 7 passed  (undici-runtime — 5 existing + 2 new)
  ```

- `pnpm exec tsgo --project tsconfig.json --noEmit` — no type errors on changed files.

- The final diff is 13 production lines across 2 files (`undici-runtime.ts`, `node-proxy-agent.ts`)
  plus a 60-line test harness across 2 test files (4 new test cases, no existing tests altered).

- No config, SDK, CLI, docs, or changelog surface was added. The new constants are
  internal-only defaults gated behind `?? undefined` / `=== Infinity` checks so callers
  with explicit `agentOptions` / `clientFactory` limits see zero behavior change.

- Both test files pass on an isolated `vitest --run` invocation without flaky retries
  (10 tests, one shard each, clean single-pass output).

- The change is bounded to the two `net/` modules that already own outbound connection
  policy; no plugin, channel, gateway, or provider code was touched.
